# Mycohobo — Noah Siegel

> Noah Siegel is one of America's leading field mycologists — a published author, award-winning photographer, and sought-after speaker with over 30 years of experience studying fungi.

## About Noah
Noah Siegel is an expert in US field mycology specializing in identification, taxonomy, and photography. He has conducted field work across the United States, Canada, New Zealand, Australia, Cameroon, Guyana, and Tanzania. He is a Curator on iNaturalist with 10,367 observations, 55,352 identifications, and 1,984 species documented.

## Books
- Mushrooms of Cascadia (2023) — Noah Siegel & Christian Schwarz, Backcountry Press, 576 pages, 750+ species
- Mushrooms of Alaska (2025) — Steve Trudell, Noah Siegel & Kate Mohatt, Timber Press, 572 pages, 400+ species
- Mushrooms of the Redwood Coast (2016) — Noah Siegel & Christian Schwarz, Ten Speed Press, 608 pages, 700+ species

## Expertise
- Field mycology and mushroom identification
- Fungal taxonomy (Cortinarius, Boletaceae, tropical fungi)
- Mushroom photography (NAMA award winner)
- Public speaking and workshops
- Biological surveys and Forest Service consulting
- Chimp mycophagy research (Issa Valley, Tanzania)

## Contact
- Email: noahmorrissiegel@gmail.com

## Speaking
Noah is available for talks, workshops, field walks, and forays. Topics include Cascadia fungi, Redwood Coast fungi, cryptic diversity, Bankeraceae, truffles, edible/poisonous/dye mushrooms of Alaska.
